name: Bytebot Desktop
description: Drives a Bytebot desktop (https://github.com/bytebot-ai/bytebot) through `bytebotd`, its local HTTP daemon, as the SECOND provider of the swappable `computer.control` layer — the first thing that makes that layer actually swappable rather than merely marked selectable. READ THIS BEFORE SELECTING IT: bytebotd drives the desktop IT runs on, which in the shipped Bytebot product is a containerized Linux desktop, NOT the machine running Ryu. Selecting it re-points `computer.capture` / `computer.click` / `computer.type` / `computer.key` / `computer.scroll` away from your own screen (`ghost`, the declared default) and onto that desktop — the same remote-target relationship `browser.control` already has between the local Chromium sidecar and a hosted browser. It serves FIVE of the six canonical verbs: `computer.focus_app` is deliberately NOT bound, because bytebotd's `application` action takes a closed seven-value enum (firefox, 1password, thunderbird, vscode, terminal, desktop, directory) while the canonical verb takes a free-form app name, so any other name would be a schema-legal call that 400s. The app switch is still reachable natively as `bytebot.application`, whose own schema carries that enum so an illegal call cannot be composed. Requires no API key — bytebotd ships with no authentication at all, which is also why this plugin only ever addresses it over loopback. SECURITY, read before enabling: bytebotd ships with NO authentication — no auth middleware, permissive CORS — and this plugin reaches it at the fixed loopback port 9990. Its egress grant is `tool:http-egress:127.0.0.1`, which is HOST-scoped, not port-scoped: approving it grants reach to any service on loopback, not just bytebotd. Only enable this on a machine where you accept that an unauthenticated desktop-control daemon is running and reachable. TARGET: bytebotd drives the desktop IT runs on — in the shipped Bytebot product that is a containerized Linux desktop, NOT the machine running Ryu — so selecting this instead of `ghost` does not give you another way to drive your own computer.
tagline: Swap computer control onto a Bytebot desktop

config.description: Capture the Bytebot desktop as a PNG. Returns `{image}`, base64-encoded, with no accessibility metadata — Bytebot's daemon is pixels-only, so target coordinates by looking at the image. Requires a reachable bytebotd at 127.0.0.1:9990.

Move the pointer to a coordinate on the Bytebot desktop and click. `button` and `clickCount` are required by the daemon and defaulted here to a single left click. Answers `{status, body}` rather than the raw upstream payload: this action returns an EMPTY body on success, and an unwrapped empty string reads like a failure. Requires a reachable bytebotd at 127.0.0.1:9990.

coordinates.description: Where to click, in screen pixels.

button.description: Which mouse button (daemon default when omitted: left).

clickCount.description: How many clicks; 2 is a double-click. Bytebot spaces repeats 150ms apart.

config.description: Type literal text into whatever has keyboard focus on the Bytebot desktop. Answers `{status, body}` because the action returns an empty body on success. Requires a reachable bytebotd at 127.0.0.1:9990.

delay.description: Milliseconds between keystrokes; slower typing is more reliable in apps that debounce input.

config.description: Press keys together as one chord on the Bytebot desktop — the daemon presses every key, then releases every key. This is `type_keys`, NOT the daemon's `press_keys`: that one holds keys down or releases them as a half-action, so a chord sent through it would leave modifiers physically held. Answers `{status, body}` because the action returns an empty body on success. Requires a reachable bytebotd at 127.0.0.1:9990.

keys.description: Key tokens pressed together, e.g. ["ctrl", "s"] or ["escape"].

delay.description: Milliseconds to hold the chord before release.

config.description: Scroll the Bytebot desktop at the pointer's current position. `scrollCount` counts MOUSE-WHEEL TICKS, not pixels, and the daemon sleeps 150ms between ticks — so it is capped low on purpose: a value meant as pixels would wedge the desktop for minutes. Answers `{status, body}` because the action returns an empty body on success. Requires a reachable bytebotd at 127.0.0.1:9990.

scrollCount.description: Number of wheel ticks (daemon requires it; defaulted to 3 here).

config.description: Focus (or launch) one of the applications preinstalled on the Bytebot desktop. The name is a CLOSED enum the daemon validates — it is not an arbitrary app name — which is exactly why the canonical `computer.focus_app` verb is not bound to this tool. `desktop` minimises everything to show the desktop. Answers `{status, body}` because the action returns an empty body on success. Requires a reachable bytebotd at 127.0.0.1:9990.

application.description: Which preinstalled application to bring to the front.
